source.original_text:
E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma-algebra; i ranges over a finite index type of size J.
V is C2, kappa>=1, and kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D2V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for all x,v. Its actual gradient vanishes at the supplied xstar.
0<eta<=c<1, eps>0, h>=0, M>=0, S>=0. The incoming probability law nu on (X,P) has integrable ||X-xstar||^2+||P||^2, with integral at most M.
The supplied deterministic nodes satisfy |t_i|<=1 and each supplied omega row satisfies sum_j |omega_ij|<=S. Position and momentum weights are arbitrary supplied real arrays; source Chebyshev quadrature is not instantiated.
For the full independent driving law gamma=(Gaussian zeta0 product Gaussian zeta1) product (Gaussian array G0 product Gaussian array G1), and mu=nu product gamma, set a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), MR=M+(1-exp(-h))*d, B=6MR+3eps^2+3eta*d and C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c), d=finrank(E). There exist the same measurable exact proximal map p, actual stopped output q and natural index N, with p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y, ||q(y)-p(y)||<=eps and run(grad V,eta,eps,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1) for every y. Define P0=aP+sigma zeta0, Y0_i=X+t_i P0, Z0_j=grad V(q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta) G0_j), Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j, Z1_j=grad V(q(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta) G1_j), and Phi=(X+h P0-sum_j positionWeight_j Z1_j, a(P0-sum_j momentumWeight_j Z1_j)+sigma zeta1). Phi is measurable and gives a Markov kernel K(s)=gamma.map(z -> Phi(s,z)). For every i both gradient squares are integrable, with E_mu||grad V(Y0_i)||^2<=2MR and E_mu||grad V(Y1_i)||^2<=4MR+2S^2 B. Both actual counts N(Y0_i)+1 and N(Y1_i)+1 are integrable; their respective expectations are at most C[1+log(1+sqrt(2MR)/eps)] and C[1+log(1+sqrt(4MR+2S^2 B)/eps)].

{E ι : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [Fintype ι]
{V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ≥0}
    (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, (κ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ ‖v‖^2)
    {eta c eps : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) (hec : eta ≤ c) (hc : c < 1) (heps : 0 < eps)
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (xstar : E) (hstar : gradient V xstar = 0)
    {h M S : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h) (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hS : 0 ≤ S)
    (hstateI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1-xstar‖^2 + ‖s.2‖^2) ν)
    (hstate : (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1-xstar‖^2 + ‖s.2‖^2 ∂ν) ≤ M)
    (t : ι → ℝ) (ht : ∀ i, |t i| ≤ 1) (omega : ι → ι → ℝ)
    (hrow : ∀ i, (∑ j, |omega i j|) ≤ S)
    (positionWeight momentumWeight : ι → ℝ) :
    let a := Real.exp (-h/2)
    let sigma := Real.sqrt (1-Real.exp (-h))
    let gi := Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)
    let γ := ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian E)).prod (gi.prod gi)
    let μ := ν.prod γ
    let MR := M + (1-Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)
    let B := 6*MR + 3*eps^2 + 3*eta*(Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)
    let C := 2 + (1+Real.log ((1-c)⁻¹))/(-Real.log c)
    ∃ p q : E → E, ∃ N : E → ℕ,
      Measurable p ∧ Measurable q ∧ Measurable N ∧
      (∀ y, p y + eta • gradient V (p y) = y ∧ ‖q y-p y‖ ≤ eps ∧
        run (gradient V) eta eps y (N y+1) y =
          some (q y,N y+1)) ∧
      let P0 := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) =>
        a • w.1.2 + sigma • w.2.1.1
      let Y0 := fun i w => w.1.1 + t i • P0 w
      let Z0 := fun j w => gradient V (q (Y0 j w) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.1 j)
      let Y1 := fun i w => Y0 i w - ∑ j, omega i j • Z0 j w
      let Z1 := fun j w => gradient V (q (Y1 j w) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.2 j)
      let Φ := fun w => (w.1.1 + h • P0 w - ∑ j, positionWeight j • Z1 j w,
        a • (P0 w - ∑ j, momentumWeight j • Z1 j w) + sigma • w.2.1.2)
      Measurable Φ ∧ ∃ K : Kernel (E × E) (E × E), IsMarkovKernel K ∧
      (∀ s, K s = γ.map (fun z => Φ (s,z))) ∧
      (∀ i, Integrable (fun w => ‖gradient V (Y0 i w)‖^2) μ ∧
        (∫ w, ‖gradient V (Y0 i w)‖^2 ∂μ) ≤ 2*MR ∧
        Integrable (fun w => (N (Y0 i w) : ℝ)+1) μ ∧
        (∫ w, (N (Y0 i w) : ℝ)+1 ∂μ) ≤
          C*(1+Real.log (1+Real.sqrt (2*MR)/eps))) ∧
      (∀ i, Integrable (fun w => ‖gradient V (Y1 i w)‖^2) μ ∧
        (∫ w, ‖gradient V (Y1 i w)‖^2 ∂μ) ≤ 4*MR+2*S^2*B ∧
        Integrable (fun w => (N (Y1 i w) : ℝ)+1) μ ∧
        (∫ w, (N (Y1 i w) : ℝ)+1 ∂μ) ≤
          C*(1+Real.log (1+Real.sqrt (4*MR+2*S^2*B)/eps)))

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel measurable structure, and let I be any finite index type. Let V:E->R be C^2 and kappa be a nonnegative real with 1<=kappa. Assume for every x,v in E that
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Fix real eta,c,epsilon with 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0. Let nu be a probability measure on E x E, and fix xstar in E with grad V(xstar)=0. Fix h,M,S>=0, and assume that the function (x,r) -> ||x-xstar||^2+||r||^2 is integrable under nu with integral at most M. Let t:I->R satisfy |t_i|<=1 for every i, and omega:I x I->R satisfy sum_j |omega_ij|<=S for every i. Let b,d:I->R be arbitrary deterministic real arrays, denoting positionWeight and momentumWeight.
Write D=dim_R E, a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), G for the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on E, gi=product_I G, gamma=(G x G) x (gi x gi), and mu=nu x gamma. Thus, under mu, an incoming state (x,r) of law nu is independent of mutually independent standard Gaussian vectors u,v and independent standard Gaussian arrays xi,xi-prime. Define the exact constants
  MR=M+(1-exp(-h))D,
  B=6 MR+3 epsilon^2+3 eta D,
  C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c).
Then there exist measurable p,q:E->E and N:E->N such that for every y in E,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  run(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1).
The exact-real interpreter returns none at zero fuel. With positive fuel it evaluates g(x), sets next=y-eta g(x), and returns (x,1) if ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon. Otherwise it recurses from next with one less fuel and adds one to a successful returned count. Thus the displayed run equality records a successful run initialized at y, with fuel and reported gradient-test count both N(y)+1, including the final successful test.
For these same witnesses, for w=((x,r),((u,v),(xi,xi-prime))) define
  P0(w)=a r+sigma u,
  Y0_i(w)=x+t_i P0(w),
  Z0_j(w)=grad V(q(Y0_j(w))+sqrt(eta)xi_j),
  Y1_i(w)=Y0_i(w)-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j(w),
  Z1_j(w)=grad V(q(Y1_j(w))+sqrt(eta)xi-prime_j),
  Phi(w)=(x+h P0(w)-sum_j b_j Z1_j(w),
          a(P0(w)-sum_j d_j Z1_j(w))+sigma v).
Then Phi is jointly measurable, and there exists a Markov kernel K from E x E to E x E such that for every incoming state s,
  K(s)=(z -> Phi(s,z))_* gamma.
In addition, for every i in I, all of the following hold with integration over w under mu:
  ||grad V(Y0_i)||^2 is integrable,
  integral ||grad V(Y0_i)||^2 dmu <= 2 MR,
  N(Y0_i)+1 is integrable,
  integral (N(Y0_i)+1) dmu <= C[1+log(1+sqrt(2 MR)/epsilon)],
  ||grad V(Y1_i)||^2 is integrable,
  integral ||grad V(Y1_i)||^2 dmu <= 4 MR+2 S^2 B,
  N(Y1_i)+1 is integrable,
  integral (N(Y1_i)+1) dmu <= C[1+log(1+sqrt(4 MR+2 S^2 B)/epsilon)].
Counts are cast to the reals in integrability and integral statements. Integrability is Bochner integrability, and all sums range over the entire finite index type. Each K(s) is a probability measure, with measurable dependence on s for every measurable output event. The theorem supplies these witnesses, the transition kernel, and these per-index input-gradient moment and interpreter-count bounds. It does not assert an invariant law, sampler convergence, final-state moment or bias bound, or an overall algorithmic gradient-call bound including the Z0 and Z1 evaluations.

/-! Algorithm 3.1 / D.4: both actual query layers under the full phase law.
The incoming state L2 budget is explicit. Neither run-wide D.7, the source
quadrature adapter, whole-phase direct-query execution count nor D.8 is closed.

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped NNReal BigOperators

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ImplementedPhaseWork

private theorem first_input_projection_preserving
    {E ι : Type*} [MeasurableSpace E] [Fintype ι]
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (g : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure g] :
    let gi := Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => g)
    MeasurePreserving
      (fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) =>
        ((w.1, w.2.1.1), w.2.2.1))
      (ν.prod ((g.prod g).prod (gi.prod gi))) ((ν.prod g).prod gi) := by
  dsimp only
  let gi := Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => g)
  have hf : MeasurePreserving Prod.fst (g.prod g) g := measurePreserving_fst
  have ha : MeasurePreserving Prod.fst (gi.prod gi) gi := measurePreserving_fst
  have hn := hf.prod ha
  have hs := (MeasurePreserving.id ν).prod hn
  have hback := MeasurePreserving.symm MeasurableEquiv.prodAssoc
    (measurePreserving_prodAssoc ν g gi)
  exact hback.comp hs

variable {E ι : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [Fintype ι]

/-- The same q/N supplies the full Gaussian phase kernel, both actual queried
gradient moments and both actual proximal query-count expectations. The only
moment hypothesis is on the incoming state, before the first half-refresh. -/
theorem implemented_phase_query_moments_and_work {V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ≥0}
    (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, (κ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ ‖v‖^2)
    {eta c eps : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) (hec : eta ≤ c) (hc : c < 1) (heps : 0 < eps)
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (xstar : E) (hstar : gradient V xstar = 0)
    {h M S : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h) (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hS : 0 ≤ S)
    (hstateI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1-xstar‖^2 + ‖s.2‖^2) ν)
    (hstate : (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1-xstar‖^2 + ‖s.2‖^2 ∂ν) ≤ M)
    (t : ι → ℝ) (ht : ∀ i, |t i| ≤ 1) (omega : ι → ι → ℝ)
    (hrow : ∀ i, (∑ j, |omega i j|) ≤ S)
    (positionWeight momentumWeight : ι → ℝ) :
    let a := Real.exp (-h/2)
    let sigma := Real.sqrt (1-Real.exp (-h))
    let gi := Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)
    let γ := ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian E)).prod (gi.prod gi)
    let μ := ν.prod γ
    let MR := M + (1-Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)
    let B := 6*MR + 3*eps^2 + 3*eta*(Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)
    let C := 2 + (1+Real.log ((1-c)⁻¹))/(-Real.log c)
    ∃ p q : E → E, ∃ N : E → ℕ,
      Measurable p ∧ Measurable q ∧ Measurable N ∧
      (∀ y, p y + eta • gradient V (p y) = y ∧ ‖q y-p y‖ ≤ eps ∧
        ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery (gradient V) eta eps y (N y+1) y =
          some (q y,N y+1)) ∧
      let P0 := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) =>
        a • w.1.2 + sigma • w.2.1.1
      let Y0 := fun i w => w.1.1 + t i • P0 w
      let Z0 := fun j w => gradient V (q (Y0 j w) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.1 j)
      let Y1 := fun i w => Y0 i w - ∑ j, omega i j • Z0 j w
      let Z1 := fun j w => gradient V (q (Y1 j w) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.2 j)
      let Φ := fun w => (w.1.1 + h • P0 w - ∑ j, positionWeight j • Z1 j w,
        a • (P0 w - ∑ j, momentumWeight j • Z1 j w) + sigma • w.2.1.2)
      Measurable Φ ∧ ∃ K : Kernel (E × E) (E × E), IsMarkovKernel K ∧
      (∀ s, K s = γ.map (fun z => Φ (s,z))) ∧
      (∀ i, Integrable (fun w => ‖gradient V (Y0 i w)‖^2) μ ∧
        (∫ w, ‖gradient V (Y0 i w)‖^2 ∂μ) ≤ 2*MR ∧
        Integrable (fun w => (N (Y0 i w) : ℝ)+1) μ ∧
        (∫ w, (N (Y0 i w) : ℝ)+1 ∂μ) ≤
          C*(1+Real.log (1+Real.sqrt (2*MR)/eps))) ∧
      (∀ i, Integrable (fun w => ‖gradient V (Y1 i w)‖^2) μ ∧
        (∫ w, ‖gradient V (Y1 i w)‖^2 ∂μ) ≤ 4*MR+2*S^2*B ∧
        Integrable (fun w => (N (Y1 i w) : ℝ)+1) μ ∧
        (∫ w, (N (Y1 i w) : ℝ)+1 ∂μ) ≤
          C*(1+Real.log (1+Real.sqrt (4*MR+2*S^2*B)/eps))) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let gi := Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)
  let γ := ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian E)).prod (gi.prod gi)
  let μ := ν.prod γ
  let μ0 := (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)).prod gi
  let proj := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) =>
    ((w.1,w.2.1.1),w.2.2.1)
  have hproj : MeasurePreserving proj μ μ0 :=
    first_input_projection_preserving ν (stdGaussian E)
  obtain ⟨hMR,hX0,hP0,hsI0,hs0,hG0,hGI0,hGint0⟩ :=
    PicardInputLaw.partial_refresh_with_picard_innovations (ι := ι) ν xstar hh hM hstateI hstate
  let X := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) => w.1.1
  let P := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) =>
    Real.exp (-h/2) • w.1.2 + Real.sqrt (1-Real.exp (-h)) • w.2.1.1
  let G := fun (j : ι) (w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E)))) =>
    w.2.2.1 j
  have hsI : Integrable (fun w => ‖X w-xstar‖^2 + ‖P w‖^2) μ :=
    hproj.integrable_comp_of_integrable hsI0
  have hs : (∫ w, ‖X w-xstar‖^2 + ‖P w‖^2 ∂μ) ≤
      M + (1-Real.exp (-h))*(Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
    calc
      _ = ∫ u : ((E × E) × E) × (ι → E), ‖u.1.1.1-xstar‖^2 +
          ‖Real.exp (-h/2) • u.1.1.2 + Real.sqrt (1-Real.exp (-h)) • u.1.2‖^2 ∂μ0 := by
        rw [← hproj.map_eq, integral_map hproj.measurable.aemeasurable (by fun_prop)]
      _ ≤ _ := hs0
  have hGI (j) : Integrable (fun w => ‖G j w‖^2) μ :=
    hproj.integrable_comp_of_integrable (hGI0 j)
  have hGint (j) : (∫ w, ‖G j w‖^2 ∂μ) ≤ (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
    calc
      _ = ∫ u : ((E × E) × E) × (ι → E), ‖u.2 j‖^2 ∂μ0 := by
        rw [← hproj.map_eq, integral_map hproj.measurable.aemeasurable (by fun_prop)]
      _ ≤ _ := le_of_eq (hGint0 j)
  obtain ⟨p,q,N,hp,hq,hN,hall,hphase⟩ :=
    ImplementedPhaseKernel.implemented_phase_kernel hκ hV hH heta hec hc heps h hh
      t omega positionWeight momentumWeight
  obtain ⟨p',N',q',hp',hN',hq',hfix',hrun',hm0,hz0,hm1⟩ :=
    PicardCenterMoment.picard_center_gradient_moment hκ hV hH heta hec hc heps μ
      X P (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) xstar hstar t ht G (fun _ => by fun_prop)
      omega hMR hS hsI hs hGI hGint hrow
  have hid (y) := ProximalExecutionIdentity.successful_query_unique
    (gradient V) eta eps y (hall y).2.2 (hrun' y).2
  have hqeq : q = q' := funext fun y => congrArg Prod.fst (hid y)
  have hNeq : N = N' := funext fun y => Nat.add_right_cancel (congrArg Prod.snd (hid y))
  subst q'
  subst N'
  obtain ⟨hvar,hΦ,K,hK,hKlaw⟩ := hphase
  have hg : Measurable (gradient V) := by
    unfold gradient
    exact ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm.continuous.comp
      (hV.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num))).measurable
  have hC : 0 ≤ 2+(1+Real.log ((1-c)⁻¹))/(-Real.log c) := by
    have hcp := heta.trans_le hec
    have hd : 0 < 1-c := sub_pos.mpr hc
    have hi : 1 ≤ (1-c)⁻¹ := (one_le_inv₀ hd).mpr (by linarith)
    have hl := Real.log_nonneg hi
    have ha := neg_pos.mpr (Real.log_neg hcp hc)
    positivity
  refine ⟨p,q,N,hp,hq,hN,hall,hΦ,K,hK,hKlaw,?_,?_⟩
  · intro i
    obtain ⟨hcI,hcB⟩ := RealizedProximalWork.realized_proximal_expected_work μ
      hκ hV hH heta hec hc heps q N (fun y => (hall y).2.2)
      (fun w => X w+t i • P w) (by fun_prop) (hm0 i).1
    refine ⟨(hm0 i).1,(hm0 i).2,hcI,hcB.trans ?_⟩
    apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ hC
    apply add_le_add_right
    apply Real.log_le_log (by positivity)
    gcongr
    exact (hm0 i).2
  · intro i
    obtain ⟨hcI,hcB⟩ := RealizedProximalWork.realized_proximal_expected_work μ
      hκ hV hH heta hec hc heps q N (fun y => (hall y).2.2)
      (fun w => X w+t i • P w - ∑ j, omega i j •
        gradient V (q (X w+t j • P w) + Real.sqrt eta • G j w))
      (by fun_prop) (hm1 i).1
    refine ⟨(hm1 i).1,(hm1 i).2,hcI,hcB.trans ?_⟩
    apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ hC
    apply add_le_add_right
    apply Real.log_le_log (by positivity)
    gcongr
    exact (hm1 i).2

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ImplementedPhaseWork

assumptions: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma-algebra; i ranges over a finite index type of size J.

lesson.statement: For the full independent driving law gamma=(Gaussian zeta0 product Gaussian zeta1) product (Gaussian array G0 product Gaussian array G1), and mu=nu product gamma, set a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), MR=M+(1-exp(-h))*d, B=6MR+3eps^2+3eta*d and C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c), d=finrank(E). There exist the same measurable exact proximal map p, actual stopped output q and natural index N, with p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y, ||q(y)-p(y)||<=eps and run(grad V,eta,eps,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1) for every y. Define P0=aP+sigma zeta0, Y0_i=X+t_i P0, Z0_j=grad V(q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta) G0_j), Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j, Z1_j=grad V(q(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta) G1_j), and Phi=(X+h P0-sum_j positionWeight_j Z1_j, a(P0-sum_j momentumWeight_j Z1_j)+sigma zeta1). Phi is measurable and gives a Markov kernel K(s)=gamma.map(z -> Phi(s,z)). For every i both gradient squares are integrable, with E_mu||grad V(Y0_i)||^2<=2MR and E_mu||grad V(Y1_i)||^2<=4MR+2S^2 B. Both actual counts N(Y0_i)+1 and N(Y1_i)+1 are integrable; their respective expectations are at most C[1+log(1+sqrt(2MR)/eps)] and C[1+log(1+sqrt(4MR+2S^2 B)/eps)].
lesson.formula: M_R=M+(1-e^{-h})d,\quad B=6M_R+3\varepsilon^2+3\eta d,\quad A_0=2M_R,\quad A_1=4M_R+2S^2B,\quad \mathbb E_\mu[N(Y_i^k)+1]\le C_c[1+\log(1+\sqrt{A_k}/\varepsilon)],\quad k=0,1.

steps.title: Marginalize the full innovation law exactly
steps.text: Project ((state,(zeta0,zeta1)),(G0,G1)) to ((state,zeta0),G0). Probability-product first-coordinate projections preserve measure. Their product, followed by inverse product association, gives exactly the input law (nu product Gaussian) product Gaussian-array. Thus omitted zeta1 and G1 factors integrate to one; independence is present in the law, not inferred from TV closeness.

steps.title: Derive the corrected refresh and Gaussian budgets
steps.text: Apply the compiled input-law theorem to the incoming state law and the first half-refresh. Pull its L2 integrability and bound, and the exact Gaussian coordinate second moments, back along the measure-preserving projection. The refreshed budget is MR, including the positive innovation contribution (1-exp(-h))*d. The proof does not silently reuse M after adding noise.

steps.title: Identify the successful queries used by both parents
steps.text: The implemented-phase theorem supplies p,q,N and the complete phase map/kernel. The Picard-center theorem supplies another successful stopped q and N along with its moment conclusions. At every y, deterministic successful-execution uniqueness equates both returned pairs. Projection of that equality and natural-number cancellation identify q and N pointwise, so the center bounds now concern exactly the kernel witnesses. The exact proximal witnesses p need not be identified.

steps.title: Use both actual Picard-center moments
steps.text: Apply the existing normalized-Hessian moment theorem under the full actual law using the derived refreshed state budget, full Gaussian G0 coordinates, supplied node bounds and row l1 bound. It gives the first-center bound 2MR, the first queried-gradient bound B, and the second-center bound 4MR+2S^2B. In particular neither actual-center gradient-square integrability nor its numerical bound is a premise.
steps.formula: \mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^0)\|^2\le2M_R,\quad\mathbb E\|Z_j^0\|^2\le B,\quad\mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^1)\|^2\le4M_R+2S^2B.

steps.title: Bound the same actual query count in each layer
steps.text: The C2 gradient and all finite phase-center maps are measurable. Apply the same-implementation expected-work theorem to each actual center under mu with the newly derived square-gradient integrability. Its count is N(Y)+1, including the final successful test. Since C>=0 and eps>0, monotonicity of square root and logarithm replaces the actual gradient moment by each derived numerical upper bound. Count integrability is a conclusion, and no different-law cost comparison is used.
steps.formula: M_R=M+(1-e^{-h})d,\quad B=6M_R+3\varepsilon^2+3\eta d,\quad A_0=2M_R,\quad A_1=4M_R+2S^2B,\quad \mathbb E_\mu[N(Y_i^k)+1]\le C_c[1+\log(1+\sqrt{A_k}/\varepsilon)],\quad k=0,1.

steps.title: Return the same full phase and both per-node costs
steps.text: Keep the measurable complete phase map and its canonical Gaussian pushforward Markov kernel from the implementation parent, together with the identified witnesses and both moment/work conclusions. The second array G1 and final refresh zeta1 remain in this phase law even though only the first-array marginal is needed to bound its second-layer centers. This does not yet sum executable per-phase gradient queries or iterate the state bound over a run.
